title: The oldest bar in every state
byline: Talia Lakritz, Erin McDowell, James LaForge
excerpt: Some of the nation's oldest bars, taverns, and saloons date before the US even declared independence. See each state's oldest bar.
content_html:
As the United States marks its 250th birthday this year, Americans are taking part in classic traditions like fireworks and barbecues.

However, few traditions are as time-honored as going to the bar.

There are more than 40,000 drinking places in the US, according to the 2023 Census. These bars come in all shapes and sizes, but some stand out for their age, with a few even predating the country itself. The White Horse Tavern in Newport, Rhode Island, opened in 1673 and is the oldest bar in the US, according to Condé Nast Traveler.

Although other states' oldest bars aren't quite as old, they still hold multiple centuries' worth of history.

Business Insider compiled a list of every state's oldest bar still in operation. Many bars claim to be the oldest in their respective states: Some are housed in historic buildings that became bars later on, while others pride themselves on the title of longest continuously running bar.

But for this list, we focused on bars that were the oldest from when they began operation as a tavern, saloon, or bar, rather than the age of the building where they're located. Bars that began in other locations or out of state were excluded. Ownership and name changes didn't automatically disqualify a bar, so long as it could trace its identity to the original establishment in one way or another.

We also included bars that were once repurposed or closed for a period of time. Some of the bars on this list continued operating as speakeasies during Prohibition, while others closed. Some were destroyed by disasters, such as fires, but were rebuilt and reopened.

See every state's oldest bar.

ALASKA: Imperial Bar, Juneau

While B&B Bar in Kodiak claims to have the oldest liquor license in the state from 1906, the Imperial Bar in Juneau was established in 1891 as the Missouri Saloon.

The bar closed during Prohibition, serving as a cigar store and a billiard parlor, the Juneau Independent reported. After national Prohibition ended in 1933, the bar's owner quickly obtained one of the first liquor licenses in the state. The Imperial Bar's website says the establishment has "survived fires, shootouts and bar fights."

ARIZONA: The Palace Restaurant and Saloon, Prescott

Opened in 1877, The Palace Restaurant and Saloon in Prescott is the oldest frontier saloon in Arizona and one of the oldest restaurants in the state, according to Prescott's tourism office. Located in Prescott's iconic "Whiskey Row," the Palace welcomed the frontiersmen Wyatt Earp, Virgil Earp, and Doc Holliday among its early patrons.

In 1900, the Palace was destroyed by the Whiskey Row fire, but it was rebuilt and open for business again within a year.

ARKANSAS: The Ohio Club, Hot Springs

Open since 1905, the Ohio Club holds the title of Arkansas' oldest bar. Many well-known figures are said to have stopped by the watering hole and casino, including gangsters Al Capone, Bugsy Siegel, Bugs Moran, and Lucky Luciano.

During Prohibition, the Ohio Club turned into a speakeasy and changed its name to Ohio Cigar Store, according to the bar's website. In front, visitors would find an unassuming cigar store, but behind a couple of doors in the back, there was a bar, as well as an upstairs casino.

CALIFORNIA: Golden Gate Saloon, Grass Valley

In 1852, the bar was filled by "thousands of thirsty prospectors," its website notes. After a devastating fire a few years later, its owners continued to sell drinks from a tent.

In 1862, the Holbrooke Hotel was built around the bar, according to California State Parks.

Another bar frequently cited as the state's oldest, the Iron Door Saloon in Groveland, didn't become a bar until 1896.

COLORADO: The Buffalo Rose, Golden

The Buffalo Rose traces its history to the International Bowling Saloon, which opened on the property in 1859, according to Uncover Colorado.

Over the years, the institution has undergone multiple ownership and structural changes. The second floor was removed in the 1880s when the owner at the time installed a large organ that wouldn't have fit otherwise, per the bar's website.

CONNECTICUT: The Griswold Inn, Essex

The Griswold Inn is practically as old as America itself. The inn has been operating since 1776 in the small Connecticut town of Essex.

For some bonus history: The building now used as the Tap Room dates back even earlier, to 1735, when it was used as a schoolhouse, the bar's website says.

DELAWARE: Kelly's Logan House, Wilmington

While not the oldest building that houses a bar in Delaware — that honor goes to Jessop's Tavern in New Castle — Kelly's Logan House is the oldest-operating restaurant and bar in the state. It's also the oldest bar in the US continually operated by the same family, Delaware Today reported.

Opened in 1864, the Irish bar and restaurant is on the National Register of Historic Places and has been a go-to spot in Delaware for St. Patrick's Day celebrations for more than 150 years. 

FLORIDA: The Palace Saloon, Fernandina Beach

The Palace Saloon sits near the Florida-Georgia border and was originally built in 1878 as a haberdashery, according to Amelia Island Hospitality Group, which now operates the bar. It was purchased and repurposed as a bar in 1903, and the new owner enlisted the help of Adolphus Busch — the founder of Anheuser-Busch — to help design it.

The bar continued to market itself as a "gentleman's establishment," offering patrons complimentary towels and 14-pound solid brass spittoons.

The Palace was also reportedly the last bar to close on the eve of Prohibition, sustaining itself as an ice cream parlor during America's dry era, per Visit Florida.

GEORGIA: The Pirate's House, Savannah

The Pirate's House opened in 1753 as a rest stop for seafarers and pirates, according to its website.

Not only is The Pirate's House Georgia's oldest bar, but parts of the building date back to 1734. After World War II, the building was set to be demolished after a period of inactivity, but it was renovated instead.

HAWAII: La Mariana Sailing Club, Honolulu

Thanks to the recent closure of Smith's Union Bar in Honolulu, which opened in 1934 and was widely known as Hawaii's oldest bar, the title is up for debate in the state.

Murphy's Bar, which opened in Honolulu in 1987, operates out of what was the Royal Saloon building, which dates back to the 19th century, but it has little connection to the original establishment, so it can't be characterized as the state's oldest bar.

Arnold's Beach Bar is another potentially historic bar. According to KHON2, the bar opened in 1933, but its opening date is more widely reported as 1992.

That leaves another Honolulu bar, La Mariana Sailing Club, which may claim the title. The bar and restaurant have been open since 1957, operating out of a new location since 1975 after a tsunami destroyed the original site, the National Trust for Historic Preservation reported.

IDAHO: Ford's Bar in Idaho Falls

One local saying is "you haven't partied until you've been to Ford's," according to East Idaho News.

Ford's opened in 1906 and has passed through multiple owners.

ILLINOIS: The Village Tavern, Long Grove

Established in 1847, The Village Tavern in Long Grove is also the oldest tavern and restaurant in continuous operation in all of Illinois.

The bar and restaurant is home to a massive 35-foot-long mahogany "Presidents Bar," which was saved after a 1967 fire, Food Republic reported.

INDIANA: Knickerbocker Saloon, Lafayette

The Knickerbocker Saloon has been in business since 1835, according to its website. Over the years, it's reportedly had notable visitors such as President Ulysses S. Grant, Mark Twain, Al Capone, and Neil Armstrong.

IOWA: Breitbach's Country Dining, Balltown

The oldest bar and restaurant in the state, Breitbach's Country Dining, has been in business since 1852 and was founded after a federal permit for the establishment was issued by President Millard Fillmore, according to the bar's website.

The spot has also been run by the same family for six generations. Fires burned down the building in 2007 and 2009, but business continued both times, running out of the parking lot while the building was reconstructed.

KANSAS: Hays House Restaurant and Tavern, Council Grove

Founded in 1857, Hays House Restaurant and Tavern was opened by Seth M. Hays, a grandson of pioneer Daniel Boone. Today, it stands as one of the oldest continuously operating restaurants west of the Mississippi River, according to the National Park Service.

KENTUCKY: Old Talbott Tavern, Bardstown

Built in 1779, the Old Talbott Tavern has offered food and shelter to travelers ever since. The tavern's website says it's known as "the oldest western stagecoach stop in America."

One of its most famous visitors was Daniel Boone, who, in April 1792, was subpoenaed to give a deposition at the tavern.

LOUISIANA: Old Absinthe House in New Orleans

Old Absinthe House was built in 1806 and sits in New Orleans' French Quarter, according to its website.

The bar's liquor license was acquired in 1835, and notable figures such as Mark Twain, Franklin D. Roosevelt, and Frank Sinatra were believed to have been housed there.

MAINE: Forest Gardens, Portland

Previously, Jameson Tavern in Freeport held the title of the state's oldest bar — it had served as a bar from 1801 to 2024, when it closed. The building is now a second location for the Portland-based King's Head Pub.  

Upon the tavern's closure, Forest Gardens in Portland became Maine's oldest bar. It opened in 1936, according to the Bangor Daily News. The bar saw an ownership change in 2018 and briefly changed names before returning to the long-standing Forest Gardens name.

MARYLAND: Reynolds Tavern and 1747 Pub, Annapolis

Originally opened in 1747, Reynolds Tavern spent much of the following two centuries serving other purposes, including as a bank and public library.

It returned to use as a tavern in 2000 after having been saved from proposed demolition decades earlier.

MASSACHUSETTS: Warren Tavern, Charlestown

Warren Tavern, established in 1780, is named after Joseph Warren, a Harvard-educated doctor and Patriot who died in the Battle of Bunker Hill in the Revolutionary War in 1775.

The tavern was one of the first structures built after the British burned down Charlestown in the battle, according to the tavern's website. George Washington and Paul Revere were among the tavern's patrons.

MICHIGAN: New Hudson Inn, New Hudson

The New Hudson Inn's website claims it opened in 1831, and the bar may have assisted in the Underground Railroad, according to WXYZ Detroit.

A false floor and hidden room may have been used to house formerly enslaved people journeying to Canada.

MINNESOTA: Neumann's, North St. Paul

Neumann's was established as a saloon in 1887. The bar opened a speakeasy upstairs during Prohibition, according to its website. The keyhole window was used to confirm the identity of patrons is still in place today.

MISSISSIPPI: Blue Front Cafe, Bentonia

King's Tavern, constructed in Natchez in the late 18th century, was long known as the state's oldest bar. However, since it closed in 2020, there's been debate over the oldest bar in the state.

While the building that houses the Under-The-Hill Saloon in Natchez dates back more than 200 years, it only opened as a bar in 1975, according to Wine Enthusiast. With no other well-documented frontrunners, the strongest candidate is the Blue Front Cafe in Bentonia. While more juke joint than bar, this café serves alcohol and is full of history.

Opened in 1948 by an African American couple, the establishment had to abide by local segregation laws, including not being allowed to serve Coca-Cola, according to Mississippi Blues Trail. The original couple's son, blues guitarist Jimmy "Duck" Holmes, still runs the cafe, the Associated Press reported.

MISSOURI: O'Malley's, Weston

O'Malley's is located 60 feet underground in what was the cellar of the Weston Brewing Company, which started producing and serving beer in 1842. In the 1980s, the then-owners, the O'Malleys, converted the underground cellar space into O'Malley's Pub.

The brewery, which had closed its doors during Prohibition, reopened in the 1990s and is now located in a building next door, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

MONTANA: Bale of Hay Saloon, Virginia City

The Bale of Hay Saloon, built in 1863, sat vacant for 36 years in the first half of the 20th century, per its website. Now owned by the Montana Heritage Commission, the classic watering hole offers live music and other events at this classic watering hole.

NEBRASKA: Glur's Tavern, Columbus

William "Buffalo Bill" Cody was among Glur's Tavern's famous patrons, according to Visit Nebraska. Established around 1876, the tavern's storied history earned it a spot on the National Register of Historic Places.

NEVADA: The Genoa Bar and Saloon, Genoa

The Genoa Bar and Saloon has been in business since 1853, according to Travel Nevada. Its period decor has made it a popular location for filming Hollywood movies. "The Shootist," "Charley Varrick," "Honky Tonk Man," "Misery," and "Till the River Runs Dry" were all filmed at the Genoa Bar and Saloon.

NEW HAMPSHIRE: The Inn at Hancock, Hancock

The Inn at Hancock has been in operation since 1789. Franklin Pierce, the only US president from New Hampshire, was friends with then-owner Squire Patten and was a regular guest, according to the New England Historical Society.

NEW MEXICO: Buckhorn Saloon and Opera House

El Farol in Santa Fe, which opened as a cantina in 1835, was previously the oldest restaurant and bar in the state, but it closed in 2025. Its new owners plan to open it this year with the same name, the Santa Fe New Mexican reported in April.

Buckhorn Saloon and Opera House has been around since the 1860s, and attracted prospectors after gold was found in the area, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

NEW YORK: Old '76 House, Tappan

The Old '76 House's website claims it dates back to 1668, while other sources list the bar as being constructed in the 1750s. During the Revolutionary War, the bar served as a safe house.

Also known as "Andre's Prison," the bar once held John Andre, a major in the British Army, before he was executed for conspiring with Benedict Arnold and spying on American forces.  

NEW JERSEY: Black Horse Tavern & Pub, Mendham

While the log cabin that became the Barnsboro Inn was built in 1720, it didn't become a tavern until 1776.

That leaves the Black Horse Tavern & Pub in Mendham, which was built in 1742. It is also the oldest continuously serving restaurant in the state, according to New Jersey Monthly.

When it was built, horse stables stood where the pub is now located, and the tavern was in an adjacent building on the property.

NORTH CAROLINA: Antlers Bar, Blowing Rock

The previous holder of the "oldest bar" title, The Tavern in Old Salem, was built in 1816. However, it closed its doors in 2019.

Antlers Bar, which opened in Blowing Rock in 1932, is now believed to be the oldest bar in the state.

Antlers Bar burned down after a recent fire, though its owners plan to fully reopen it. For the time being, the bar is operating out of its nearby sister restaurant, Hellbender Bed and Beverage, according to its website.

NORTH DAKOTA: Town Hall Bar, West Fargo

Peacock Alley American Grill, which first opened in 1933, recently closed, leaving the Town Hall Bar in West Fargo to claim the title of the oldest bar in North Dakota.

The bar was constructed and opened in 1935, according to KVRR.

OHIO: Ye Olde Trail Tavern, Yellow Springs

Ye Olde Trail Tavern in Yellow Springs was built by Elisha Mills and his son, William, as a tavern in 1827. It's known for its signature burgers, and is also said to be haunted by a dark-haired woman in a blue dress, per the Yellow Springs News.

OKLAHOMA: Eischen's Bar, Okarche

Peter Eischen established Eischen's Bar in 1896. The bar closed down when state prohibition began in 1907, but it was reopened by Eischen's son and grandson, according to the bar's website.

Popular dishes include fried chicken, Frito pie, and a roast beef sandwich, according to Yelp.

OREGON: Pioneer Saloon, Paisley

In Oregon, the oldest bar question has been subject to debate, according to Oregon Public Broadcasting. Two bars — the Pioneer Saloon in Paisley and the Rainbow Cafe in Pendleton — both claim to have opened in 1883.

While either could be worthy of the oldest bar title, OPB reported that one historian found an estate record for the Pioneer Saloon confirming the 1883 date. The bar itself is full of history, like its Brunswick bar, which was shipped from Boston in 1905.

PENNSYLVANIA: King George II Inn, Bristol

Broad Axe Tavern, which also opened in 1681, closed in 2019, according to KYW News Radio. This leaves the King George II Inn as the oldest in the state.

George Washington's officers once stayed at the inn, and one Pennsylvania militia general helped plan the crossing of the Delaware River inside its walls, Tasting Table reported.

RHODE ISLAND: White Horse Tavern, Newport

White Horse Tavern in Newport was called "the oldest bar in America" by Condé Nast Traveler. A National Historic Landmark, White Horse Tavern was originally built as a two-story home, according to the bar's website.

William Mayes converted it into a tavern in 1673 and held City Council meetings and court proceedings there. In the 20th century, after a long period of neglect, the property was restored by the Preservation Society of Newport County.

SOUTH CAROLINA: Henry's on the Market, Charleston

The previous oldest bar in the state, McCrady's Tavern and Long Room in Charleston, dated back to 1788, but it closed in 2020.

While Henry's on the Market isn't quite as old, it's been open since 1933.

Henry's was initially founded as a grocery store by Henry Otto Hasselmeyer, a German immigrant, according to the bar's website. After Prohibition ended, he turned it into a beer parlor.

SOUTH DAKOTA: Buffalo Bodega, Deadwood

The Buffalo Bodega was established in 1877 and named for the owner's friend and hunting buddy, Buffalo Bill Cody, according to the city of Deadwood.

TENNESSEE: Springwater Supper Club & Lounge, Nashville

Springwater, which opened in 1896, is a "true dive bar in its purest form," Jesse Baker, the bar's talent buyer, told Business Insider.

Although there have been structural updates to the bar over the past 100-plus years, there's plenty of evidence of its fascinating history. During Prohibition, the bar operated as a speakeasy and today, it still has a peephole door with an axe mark from when the fire department forced their way in "to bust heads," Baker said.

TEXAS: Scholz Garten, Austin

The bar at Scholz Garten was founded by a German immigrant and Civil War veteran, August Scholz, in 1866, according to Scholz Garten's website. It promptly became a favorite haunt of other German immigrants in the area.

When the bar was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, The New York Times reported, "As bars go, this one is anything but usual, having given long service as a watering hole, debating forum, community center and political staging point."

Today, the bar, which serves up German food and barbecue, is popular among University of Texas students.

UTAH: Shooting Star Saloon, Huntsville

The bar opened in 1879, according to the Salt Lake Tribune.

Today, it's decorated with trinkets and bills from visitors from around the world, but most eye-catching is the stuffed head of Buck, a record-setting 298-pound Saint Bernard, who was mounted on the wall after his death in 1957, per Utah Stories.

VERMONT: Ye Olde Tavern, Manchester

Ye Olde Tavern dates back to the 18th century — a sign outside reads, "Wining & Dining since 1790" — although it's been through many names and owners since then. It's had its current name since 1976. 

The town's first telephone line was installed at the tavern, according to the tavern's website. The historic building is now on the Vermont Register of Historic Places.

VIRGINIA: The Tavern, Abingdon

A few other historic buildings in Virginia are home to bars, leading to some debate on which is the oldest. The Red Fox Inn in Middleburg, for example, was reportedly established in 1728, but its National Register of Historic Places application lists the date as being built circa 1830.

The Tavern, built in 1779, is often recognized as Virginia's oldest bar, WCYB Abingdon reported. During the Civil War, it was used as a hospital, and it has also housed a post office, a bakery, a barber shop, and a general store, among other things.

WASHINGTON: Bluebird Inn, Bickleton

While there's some debate over who can claim the title of oldest bar in Washington, the Bluebird Inn in Bickleton opened its saloon in 1887, per the town's website. According to the town's Alder Creek Pioneer Carousel Museum, women were welcomed into the bar for the first time in the 1960s.

The town, known as "the bluebird capital of the world" for the number of bluebirds that call it home for most of the year, has a population of just 90 people, according to the 2020 Census.

WEST VIRGINIA: North End Tavern and Brewery, Parkersburg

The North End Tavern and Brewery, which opened in 1899, is the oldest tavern in the state. According to the West Virginia Gazette-Mail, the only remnants from the original bar are the "rough bricks laid into the basement floor" and "part of the foundation."

In the 1990s, owner Joe Roedersheimer added a brewery. These days, the bar is better known as The Net.

WISCONSIN: Landmark 1850, Milwaukee

Per OnMilwaukee, the bar initially was a stagecoach stop between Milwaukee and Racine. It opened as a bar for farmers and travelers in 1850, the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported.

The building underwent a renovation in 1983.

WYOMING: Miners and Stockmen's Steakhouse, Hartville

Miners and Stockmen's opened its doors for the first time in 1862 — that's 28 years before Wyoming was granted statehood. Fittingly, it's found in Hartville, Wyoming's oldest incorporated town still in existence, according to Platte County.

Patrons can choose from a steakhouse menu and long list of wines and whiskey, according to the bar's website.

MARYLAND: Reynolds Tavern and 1747 Pub, Annapolis The Reynolds Tavern and 1747 pub first opened in 1747. Kimberly F./Yelp Originally opened in 1747, Reynolds Tavern spent much of the following two centuries serving other purposes, including as a bank and public library.It returned to use as a tavern in 2000 after having been saved from proposed demolition decades earlier. MASSACHUSETTS: Warren Tavern, Charlestown Warren Tavern was first established in 1780. Wangkun Jia/Shutterstock Warren Tavern, established in 1780, is named after Joseph Warren, a Harvard-educated doctor and Patriot who died in the Battle of Bunker Hill in the Revolutionary War in 1775.The tavern was one of the first structures built after the British burned down Charlestown in the battle, according to the tavern's website. George Washington and Paul Revere were among the tavern's patrons. MICHIGAN: New Hudson Inn, New Hudson The New Hudson Inn claims to have opened in 1831. Mike G./Yelp The New Hudson Inn's website claims it opened in 1831, and the bar may have assisted in the Underground Railroad, according to WXYZ Detroit.A false floor and hidden room may have been used to house formerly enslaved people journeying to Canada. MINNESOTA: Neumann's, North St. Paul Neumann's has been in business since 1887. Danny A./Yelp Neumann's was established as a saloon in 1887. The bar opened a speakeasy upstairs during Prohibition, according to its website. The keyhole window was used to confirm the identity of patrons is still in place today. MISSISSIPPI: Blue Front Cafe, Bentonia The Blue Front Cafe opened in 1948. Mick Gold via Getty Images King's Tavern, constructed in Natchez in the late 18th century, was long known as the state's oldest bar. However, since it closed in 2020, there's been debate over the oldest bar in the state.While the building that houses the Under-The-Hill Saloon in Natchez dates back more than 200 years, it only opened as a bar in 1975, according to Wine Enthusiast. With no other well-documented frontrunners, the strongest candidate is the Blue Front Cafe in Bentonia. While more juke joint than bar, this café serves alcohol and is full of history.Opened in 1948 by an African American couple, the establishment had to abide by local segregation laws, including not being allowed to serve Coca-Cola, according to Mississippi Blues Trail. The original couple's son, blues guitarist Jimmy "Duck" Holmes, still runs the cafe, the Associated Press reported. MISSOURI: O'Malley's, Weston O'Malley's is housed underground in a former brewery. Rick B./Yelp O'Malley's is located 60 feet underground in what was the cellar of the Weston Brewing Company, which started producing and serving beer in 1842. In the 1980s, the then-owners, the O'Malleys, converted the underground cellar space into O'Malley's Pub.The brewery, which had closed its doors during Prohibition, reopened in the 1990s and is now located in a building next door, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation. MONTANA: Bale of Hay Saloon, Virginia City The Bale of Hay Saloon was built in 1863. Kay R./Yelp The Bale of Hay Saloon, built in 1863, sat vacant for 36 years in the first half of the 20th century, per its website. Now owned by the Montana Heritage Commission, the classic watering hole offers live music and other events at this classic watering hole. NEBRASKA: Glur's Tavern, Columbus Glur's Tavern opened in 1876. Joe H./Yelp William "Buffalo Bill" Cody was among Glur's Tavern's famous patrons, according to Visit Nebraska. Established around 1876, the tavern's storied history earned it a spot on the National Register of Historic Places. NEVADA: The Genoa Bar and Saloon, Genoa The Genoa Bar and Saloon opened in 1853. Ashley P./Yelp The Genoa Bar and Saloon has been in business since 1853, according to Travel Nevada. Its period decor has made it a popular location for filming Hollywood movies. "The Shootist," "Charley Varrick," "Honky Tonk Man," "Misery," and "Till the River Runs Dry" were all filmed at the Genoa Bar and Saloon. NEW HAMPSHIRE: The Inn at Hancock, Hancock The Inn at Hancock has been open since 1789. Joshua C./Yelp The Inn at Hancock has been in operation since 1789. Franklin Pierce, the only US president from New Hampshire, was friends with then-owner Squire Patten and was a regular guest, according to the New England Historical Society. NEW MEXICO: Buckhorn Saloon and Opera House The Buckhorn Saloon has been around since the 1860s. Christina M./Yelp El Farol in Santa Fe, which opened as a cantina in 1835, was previously the oldest restaurant and bar in the state, but it closed in 2025. Its new owners plan to open it this year with the same name, the Santa Fe New Mexican reported in April.Buckhorn Saloon and Opera House has been around since the 1860s, and attracted prospectors after gold was found in the area, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation. NEW YORK: Old '76 House, Tappan Old '76 House dates back to either the 17th or 18th century. Brian Logan Photography/Shutterstock The Old '76 House's website claims it dates back to 1668, while other sources list the bar as being constructed in the 1750s. During the Revolutionary War, the bar served as a safe house.Also known as "Andre's Prison," the bar once held John Andre, a major in the British Army, before he was executed for conspiring with Benedict Arnold and spying on American forces. NEW JERSEY: Black Horse Tavern & Pub, Mendham The Black Horse Tavern and Pub was built in 1742. Grace A./Yelp While the log cabin that became the Barnsboro Inn was built in 1720, it didn't become a tavern until 1776.That leaves the Black Horse Tavern & Pub in Mendham, which was built in 1742. It is also the oldest continuously serving restaurant in the state, according to New Jersey Monthly.When it was built, horse stables stood where the pub is now located, and the tavern was in an adjacent building on the property. NORTH CAROLINA: Antlers Bar, Blowing Rock Antlers Bar opened in 1932, and its owners plan to reopen the location after a recent fire. Stephanie J./Yelp The previous holder of the "oldest bar" title, The Tavern in Old Salem, was built in 1816. However, it closed its doors in 2019.Antlers Bar, which opened in Blowing Rock in 1932, is now believed to be the oldest bar in the state.Antlers Bar burned down after a recent fire, though its owners plan to fully reopen it. For the time being, the bar is operating out of its nearby sister restaurant, Hellbender Bed and Beverage, according to its website. NORTH DAKOTA: Town Hall Bar, West Fargo The Bonanzaville USA museum is just down the street from Town Hall Bar, which dates back to 1935. Kirkam/Shutterstock Peacock Alley American Grill, which first opened in 1933, recently closed, leaving the Town Hall Bar in West Fargo to claim the title of the oldest bar in North Dakota.The bar was constructed and opened in 1935, according to KVRR. OHIO: Ye Olde Trail Tavern, Yellow Springs Ye Olde Trail Tavern opened in 1827. Elyse F./Yelp Ye Olde Trail Tavern in Yellow Springs was built by Elisha Mills and his son, William, as a tavern in 1827. It's known for its signature burgers, and is also said to be haunted by a dark-haired woman in a blue dress, per the Yellow Springs News. OKLAHOMA: Eischen's Bar, Okarche Eischen's Bar opened in 1896. Danielle D./Yelp Peter Eischen established Eischen's Bar in 1896. The bar closed down when state prohibition began in 1907, but it was reopened by Eischen's son and grandson, according to the bar's website.Popular dishes include fried chicken, Frito pie, and a roast beef sandwich, according to Yelp. OREGON: Pioneer Saloon, Paisley The Pioneer Saloon opened in 1883. Ilona S./Yelp In Oregon, the oldest bar question has been subject to debate, according to Oregon Public Broadcasting. Two bars — the Pioneer Saloon in Paisley and the Rainbow Cafe in Pendleton — both claim to have opened in 1883.While either could be worthy of the oldest bar title, OPB reported that one historian found an estate record for the Pioneer Saloon confirming the 1883 date. The bar itself is full of history, like its Brunswick bar, which was shipped from Boston in 1905. PENNSYLVANIA: King George II Inn, Bristol The King George II Inn opened in 1681. John L./Yelp Broad Axe Tavern, which also opened in 1681, closed in 2019, according to KYW News Radio. This leaves the King George II Inn as the oldest in the state.George Washington's officers once stayed at the inn, and one Pennsylvania militia general helped plan the crossing of the Delaware River inside its walls, Tasting Table reported. RHODE ISLAND: White Horse Tavern, Newport White Horse Tavern became a tavern in 1673. Matthew Carreiro/Shutterstock White Horse Tavern in Newport was called "the oldest bar in America" by Condé Nast Traveler. A National Historic Landmark, White Horse Tavern was originally built as a two-story home, according to the bar's website.William Mayes converted it into a tavern in 1673 and held City Council meetings and court proceedings there. In the 20th century, after a long period of neglect, the property was restored by the Preservation Society of Newport County. SOUTH CAROLINA: Henry's on the Market, Charleston Henry's on the Market has been a bar since 1933. Rory B./Yelp The previous oldest bar in the state, McCrady's Tavern and Long Room in Charleston, dated back to 1788, but it closed in 2020.While Henry's on the Market isn't quite as old, it's been open since 1933.Henry's was initially founded as a grocery store by Henry Otto Hasselmeyer, a German immigrant, according to the bar's website. After Prohibition ended, he turned it into a beer parlor. SOUTH DAKOTA: Buffalo Bodega, Deadwood Buffalo Bodega Bar was established in 1877. Shutterstock/RaksyBH The Buffalo Bodega was established in 1877 and named for the owner's friend and hunting buddy, Buffalo Bill Cody, according to the city of Deadwood. TENNESSEE: Springwater Supper Club & Lounge, Nashville Springwater Supper Club & Lounge opened in the 1890s. Courtesy Springwater Supper Club & Lounge Springwater, which opened in 1896, is a "true dive bar in its purest form," Jesse Baker, the bar's talent buyer, told Business Insider.Although there have been structural updates to the bar over the past 100-plus years, there's plenty of evidence of its fascinating history. During Prohibition, the bar operated as a speakeasy and today, it still has a peephole door with an axe mark from when the fire department forced their way in "to bust heads," Baker said. TEXAS: Scholz Garten, Austin Scholz Garten opened in 1866. Carol I./Yelp The bar at Scholz Garten was founded by a German immigrant and Civil War veteran, August Scholz, in 1866, according to Scholz Garten's website. It promptly became a favorite haunt of other German immigrants in the area.When the bar was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, The New York Times reported, "As bars go, this one is anything but usual, having given long service as a watering hole, debating forum, community center and political staging point."Today, the bar, which serves up German food and barbecue, is popular among University of Texas students. UTAH: Shooting Star Saloon, Huntsville Shooting Star Saloon opened in 1879. Yelp/Alan H. The bar opened in 1879, according to the Salt Lake Tribune.Today, it's decorated with trinkets and bills from visitors from around the world, but most eye-catching is the stuffed head of Buck, a record-setting 298-pound Saint Bernard, who was mounted on the wall after his death in 1957, per Utah Stories. VERMONT: Ye Olde Tavern, Manchester Ye Olde Tavern opened in 1790. Yelp/Brandt M. Ye Olde Tavern dates back to the 18th century — a sign outside reads, "Wining & Dining since 1790" — although it's been through many names and owners since then. It's had its current name since 1976. The town's first telephone line was installed at the tavern, according to the tavern's website. The historic building is now on the Vermont Register of Historic Places. VIRGINIA: The Tavern, Abingdon The Tavern in Abingdon was built in 1779. Shutterstock/Dee Browning A few other historic buildings in Virginia are home to bars, leading to some debate on which is the oldest. The Red Fox Inn in Middleburg, for example, was reportedly established in 1728, but its National Register of Historic Places application lists the date as being built circa 1830.The Tavern, built in 1779, is often recognized as Virginia's oldest bar, WCYB Abingdon reported. During the Civil War, it was used as a hospital, and it has also housed a post office, a bakery, a barber shop, and a general store, among other things. WASHINGTON: Bluebird Inn, Bickleton The Bluebird Inn in Washington opened as a saloon in 1887. Michael G./Yelp While there's some debate over who can claim the title of oldest bar in Washington, the Bluebird Inn in Bickleton opened its saloon in 1887, per the town's website. According to the town's Alder Creek Pioneer Carousel Museum, women were welcomed into the bar for the first time in the 1960s.The town, known as "the bluebird capital of the world" for the number of bluebirds that call it home for most of the year, has a population of just 90 people, according to the 2020 Census. WEST VIRGINIA: North End Tavern and Brewery, Parkersburg The North End Tavern & Brewery dates back to 1899. Cindi R./Yelp The North End Tavern and Brewery, which opened in 1899, is the oldest tavern in the state. According to the West Virginia Gazette-Mail, the only remnants from the original bar are the "rough bricks laid into the basement floor" and "part of the foundation."In the 1990s, owner Joe Roedersheimer added a brewery. These days, the bar is better known as The Net. WISCONSIN: Landmark 1850, Milwaukee Landmark 1850. Kyrylo R./Yelp Per OnMilwaukee, the bar initially was a stagecoach stop between Milwaukee and Racine. It opened as a bar for farmers and travelers in 1850, the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported.The building underwent a renovation in 1983. WYOMING: Miners and Stockmen's Steakhouse, Hartville Miners and Stockmen's Steakhouse & Spirits opened in 1862. Courtesy Miners and Stockmen's Steakhouse & Spirits Miners and Stockmen's opened its doors for the first time in 1862 — that's 28 years before Wyoming was granted statehood. Fittingly, it's found in Hartville, Wyoming's oldest incorporated town still in existence, according to Platte County.Patrons can choose from a steakhouse menu and long list of wines and whiskey, according to the bar's website.Editor's note: This story was originally published in May 2022 and was most recently updated in July 2026 to reflect closures.

content_html_zh:
今年是美国建国 250 周年，美国人正在参与烟花和烧烤等经典传统活动。

然而，很少有传统能像去酒吧一样历史悠久。

根据 2023 年人口普查，美国有超过 40,000 个饮酒场所。 这些酒吧的形状和大小各异，但有些酒吧因其年代久远而引人注目，有一些酒吧的历史甚至早于该国本身。 据 Condé Nast Traveler 报道，位于罗德岛州纽波特的 White Horse Tavern 于 1673 年开业，是美国最古老的酒吧。

尽管其他州最古老的酒吧没有那么古老，但它们仍然拥有多个世纪的历史。

《商业内幕》编制了一份各州仍在营业的最古老酒吧的清单。 许多酒吧都声称是各自州最古老的酒吧：有些酒吧位于后来成为酒吧的历史建筑内，而另一些酒吧则以连续经营时间最长的酒吧的称号而自豪。

但在这份名单中，我们关注的是那些从开始作为小酒馆、酒吧或酒吧开始运营以来最古老的酒吧，而不是它们所在建筑的年龄。 在其他地点或州外开设的酒吧被排除在外。 所有权和名称变更并不自动取消酒吧的资格，只要它能够以某种方式追溯到其原始酒吧的身份。

我们还包括曾经改变用途或关闭一段时间的酒吧。 这份名单上的一些酒吧在禁酒令期间继续作为地下酒吧营业，而其他酒吧则关门了。 有些被火灾等灾难摧毁，但又被重建并重新开放。

参观每个州最古老的酒吧。

阿拉斯加：帝国酒吧，朱诺

科迪亚克的 B&B Bar 声称自 1906 年起就拥有该州最古老的酒类许可证，而朱诺的 Imperial Bar 则成立于 1891 年，当时名为密苏里州沙龙。

据《朱诺独立报》报道，该酒吧在禁酒令期间关闭，充当雪茄店和台球室。 1933 年全国禁酒令结束后，酒吧老板很快获得了该州首批酒类许可证之一。 帝国酒吧的网站称，该酒吧“经历了火灾、枪战和酒吧斗殴”。

亚利桑那州：宫殿餐厅和沙龙，普雷斯科特

据普雷斯科特旅游办公室介绍，普雷斯科特的 The Palace Restaurant and Saloon 于 1877 年开业，是亚利桑那州最古老的边境酒吧，也是该州最古老的餐厅之一。 这座宫殿位于普雷斯科特标志性的“威士忌街”，早期的赞助人包括拓荒者怀亚特·厄普 (Wyatt Earp)、维吉尔·厄普 (Virgil Earp) 和多克·霍利迪 (Doc Holliday)。

1900年，宫殿被威士忌街大火烧毁，但一年之内又重建并重新开放。

阿肯色州：俄亥俄俱乐部，温泉城

Ohio Club 自 1905 年开业，拥有阿肯色州最古老酒吧的称号。 据说许多知名人士都曾到过这家酒吧和赌场，包括黑帮阿尔·卡彭、巴格西·西格尔、巴格斯·莫兰和幸运卢西亚诺。

据酒吧网站称，在禁酒令期间，俄亥俄俱乐部变成了一家地下酒吧，并更名为俄亥俄雪茄店。 在前面，游客会发现一家不起眼的雪茄店，但在后面的几扇门后面，有一家酒吧，楼上还有一家赌场。

加利福尼亚州：金门轿车，草谷

1852 年，酒吧里挤满了“数千名口渴的探矿者”，其网站称。 几年后发生毁灭性火灾后，其主人继续在帐篷里出售饮料。

据加州州立公园称，1862 年，霍尔布鲁克酒店围绕酒吧而建。

格罗夫兰 (Groveland) 的 Iron Door Saloon 酒吧经常被认为是该州最古老的酒吧，直到 1896 年才成为酒吧。

科罗拉多州：水牛玫瑰，金色

据 Uncover Colorado 报道，Buffalo Rose 酒店的历史可以追溯到 1859 年在该酒店开业的国际保龄球馆 (International Bowling Saloon)。

多年来，该机构经历了多重所有权和结构变化。 据酒吧网站称，二楼在 1880 年代被拆除，当时的店主安装了一个大型风琴，否则无法安装。

康涅狄格州：格里斯沃尔德旅馆，埃塞克斯

格里斯沃尔德旅馆 (Griswold Inn) 的历史几乎与美国本身一样古老。 该旅馆自 1776 年起就在康涅狄格州小镇埃塞克斯开业。

值得一提的是，该酒吧的网站称，现在用作酒吧室的建筑的历史可以追溯到更早的 1735 年，当时它被用作校舍。

特拉华州：凯利洛根之家，威尔明顿

虽然凯利洛根之家 (Kelly's Logan House) 不是特拉华州最古老的设有酒吧的建筑（这一荣誉属于纽卡斯尔的杰索普酒馆 (Jessop's Tavern)），但它是该州最古老的经营餐厅和酒吧。 据《今日特拉华》报道，这也是美国由同一家族持续经营的最古老的酒吧。

这家爱尔兰酒吧和餐厅于 1864 年开业，已被列入国家历史名胜名录，150 多年来一直是特拉华州庆祝圣帕特里克节的首选地点。

佛罗里达州：费南迪纳比奇皇宫沙龙

据目前经营该酒吧的阿米莉亚岛酒店集团 (Amelia Island Hospitality Group) 介绍，Palace Saloon 位于佛罗里达州和佐治亚州边境附近，最初建于 1878 年，当时是一家小百货店。 1903 年，它被购买并改造成酒吧，新主人得到了安海斯-布希 (Anheuser-Busch) 创始人阿道夫·布希 (Adolphus Busch) 的帮助来设计它。

该酒吧继续将自己定位为“绅士场所”，为顾客提供免费毛巾和 14 磅重的实心黄铜痰盂。

据《佛罗里达旅游》报道，据报道，这座宫殿也是禁酒令前夕最后一家关闭的酒吧，在美国干旱时期以冰淇淋店的形式维持运转。

乔治亚州：海盗之家，萨凡纳

据其网站介绍，海盗之家于 1753 年开业，作为海员和海盗的休息站。

The Pirate's House 不仅是佐治亚州最古老的酒吧，而且该建筑的部分建筑的历史可以追溯到 1734 年。 第二次世界大战后，这座建筑在闲置一段时间后准备拆除，但后来进行了翻新。

夏威夷：拉马里亚纳帆船俱乐部，檀香山

由于檀香山的 Smith's Union Bar 于 1934 年开业，被誉为夏威夷最古老的酒吧，最近关闭了，该酒吧的名称在该州引起了争议。

Murphy's Bar 于 1987 年在檀香山开业，其前身是皇家沙龙大楼，其历史可以追溯到 19 世纪，但它与原来的建筑几乎没有联系，因此它不能被称为该州最古老的酒吧。

阿诺德海滩酒吧是另一个可能具有历史意义的酒吧。 据 KHON2 报道，该酒吧于 1933 年开业，但更广泛的报道称其开业日期为 1992 年。

剩下的另一家檀香山酒吧 La Mariana Sailing Club 可能会获得这一称号。 据国家历史保护信托基金会报道，这家酒吧和餐厅自 1957 年开始营业，1975 年海啸摧毁了原址后，在新地点营业。

爱达荷州：爱达荷福尔斯的福特酒吧

据《东爱达荷新闻》报道，当地人有句俗话：“没有去过福特汽车店，就不算参加过派对”。

福特汽车店于 1906 年开业，历经多任业主。

伊利诺伊州：乡村酒馆，朗格罗夫

位于朗格罗夫 (Long Grove) 的乡村酒馆 (The Village Tavern) 成立于 1847 年，也是伊利诺伊州持续营业的最古老的酒馆和餐厅。

据 Food Republic 报道，这家酒吧兼餐厅内有一座 35 英尺长的巨大桃花心木“总统酒吧”，该酒吧在 1967 年的一场火灾后得以幸存。

印第安纳州：Knickerbocker Saloon，拉斐特

据其网站介绍，Knickerbocker Saloon 自 1835 年以来一直营业。 据报道，多年来，这里曾接待过尤利西斯·S·总统等知名人士。 格兰特、马克·吐温、阿尔·卡彭和尼尔·阿姆斯特朗。

爱荷华州：布莱特巴赫的乡村餐厅，鲍尔敦

据酒吧网站介绍，Breitbach's Country Dining 是该州最古老的酒吧和餐厅，自 1852 年开始营业，是在总统米勒德·菲尔莫尔 (Millard Fillmore) 颁发联邦开业许可证后成立的。

该场所也由同一家族经营了六代。 2007 年和 2009 年的大火烧毁了这座建筑，但两次生意都在继续，在建筑重建期间，停车场都用完了。

堪萨斯州：Hays House 餐厅和酒馆，康瑟尔格罗夫

Hays House 餐厅和酒馆成立于 1857 年，由 Seth M. 海斯是先驱者丹尼尔·布恩的孙子。 据国家公园管理局称，如今，它是密西西比河以西最古老的持续经营的餐厅之一。

肯塔基州：老塔尔博特酒馆，巴兹敦

老塔尔博特酒馆 (Old Talbott Tavern) 建于 1779 年，从那时起就一直为旅行者提供食物和住所。 该酒馆的网站称其被称为“美国最古老的西部驿马车站”。

丹尼尔·布恩 (Daniel Boone) 是该酒馆最著名的访客之一，他于 1792 年 4 月被传唤到酒馆作证。

路易斯安那州：新奥尔良的老苦艾酒屋

据其网站介绍，老苦艾酒屋建于 1806 年，位于新奥尔良的法国区。

该酒吧于 1835 年获得酒类经营许可证，马克·吐温 (Mark Twain)、富兰克林·D. 据信罗斯福和弗兰克·辛纳屈曾住在那里。

缅因州：森林花园，波特兰

此前，自由港的 Jameson Tavern 拥有该州最古老酒吧的称号——它从 1801 年一直是一家酒吧，到 2024 年关闭为止。 该建筑现在是波特兰 King's Head 酒吧的第二个地点。

小酒馆关闭后，波特兰的森林花园成为缅因州最古老的酒吧。 据《班戈每日新闻》报道，它于 1936 年开业。 该酒吧于 2018 年发生了所有权变更，并短暂更改了名称，然后又恢复了长期存在的 Forest Gardens 名称。

马里兰州：Reynolds Tavern 和 1747 Pub，安纳波利斯

雷诺兹酒馆 (Reynolds Tavern) 最初于 1747 年开业，在接下来的两个世纪中大部分时间都用于其他目的，包括作为银行和公共图书馆。

几十年前，它从拟议的拆除中幸免于难，并于 2000 年重新作为酒馆使用。

马萨诸塞州：沃伦酒馆，查尔斯敦

沃伦酒馆 (Warren Tavern) 成立于 1780 年，以约瑟夫·沃伦 (Joseph Warren) 的名字命名。约瑟夫·沃伦是一位毕业于哈佛大学的医生，也是一位爱国者，在 1775 年独立战争的邦克山战役中阵亡。

据酒馆网站称，该酒馆是英国人在战斗中烧毁查尔斯敦后建造的第一批建筑之一。 乔治·华盛顿和保罗·里维尔是这家酒馆的常客。

密歇根州：新哈德逊旅馆，新哈德逊

据 WXYZ 底特律报道，New Hudson Inn 的网站声称其于 1831 年开业，该酒吧可能对地下铁路有所帮助。

假地板和隐藏的房间可能被用来安置前往加拿大的前奴隶。

明尼苏达州：诺伊曼，北圣保罗

Neumann's 成立于 1887 年，最初是一家酒吧。 据其网站称，该酒吧在禁酒令期间在楼上开设了一家地下酒吧。 用于确认顾客身份的钥匙孔窗户至今仍然存在。

密西西比州：Blue Front Cafe，本托尼亚

King's Tavern 建于 18 世纪末，长期以来一直被认为是该州最古老的酒吧。 然而，自 2020 年关闭以来，关于该州最古老的酒吧的争论一直存在。

据 Wine Enthusiast 介绍，虽然纳奇兹 Under-The-Hill Saloon 所在的建筑已有 200 多年的历史，但它直到 1975 年才作为酒吧开业。 由于没有其他有据可查的领先者，最有力的候选者是本托尼亚的 Blue Front Cafe。 虽然这家咖啡馆更像是点唱机酒吧而不是酒吧，但它供应酒精饮料，并且充满了历史。

据《密西西比蓝调之路》报道，这家店于 1948 年由一对非洲裔美国夫妇开设，必须遵守当地的种族隔离法，包括不得提供可口可乐。 据美联社报道，这对夫妇的儿子、布鲁斯吉他手吉米·“鸭子”·霍姆斯仍然经营着这家咖啡馆。

密苏里州：奥马利，韦斯顿

O'Malley's 位于地下 60 英尺处，这里曾是 Weston Brewing Company 的地窖，该公司于 1842 年开始生产和供应啤酒。 20 世纪 80 年代，当时的业主奥马利 (O'Malley) 夫妇将地下酒窖改造成奥马利酒吧 (O'Malley's Pub)。

据国家历史保护信托基金会称，这家啤酒厂在禁酒令期间关闭，于 20 世纪 90 年代重新开业，目前位于隔壁的一栋建筑内。

蒙大拿州：弗吉尼亚市的干草包沙龙

据其网站介绍，Bale of Hay Saloon 酒吧建于 1863 年，在 20 世纪上半叶空置了 36 年。 这个经典的酒吧现在由蒙大拿州遗产委员会所有，提供现场音乐和其他活动。

内布拉斯加州：格鲁尔酒馆，哥伦布

据内布拉斯加州旅游局报道，威廉·“水牛比尔”·科迪是格鲁尔酒馆的著名顾客之一。 该酒馆成立于 1876 年左右，其传奇的历史使其在国家历史名胜名录中占有一席之地。

内华达州：热那亚酒吧和沙龙，热那亚

据内华达旅游局介绍，热那亚酒吧和沙龙自 1853 年开始营业。 其具有时代特色的装饰使其成为好莱坞电影拍摄的热门地点。 《射击者》、《查理·瓦里克》、《Honky Tonk Man》、《Misery》和《直到河水干涸》均在热那亚酒吧和沙龙拍摄。

新罕布什尔州：汉考克旅馆, 汉考克

汉考克旅馆 (The Inn at Hancock) 自 1789 年开始营业。 据新英格兰历史学会称，富兰克林·皮尔斯是唯一一位来自新罕布什尔州的美国总统，他与当时的老板乡绅彭定康是朋友，也是这里的常客。

新墨西哥州：巴克霍恩沙龙和歌剧院

圣达菲的 El Farol 于 1835 年作为一家小酒馆开业，此前是该州最古老的餐厅和酒吧，但于 2025 年关闭。 据《新墨西哥州圣达菲》四月报道，其新主人计划今年以同名开业。

据国家历史保护信托基金会称，鹿角酒吧和歌剧院自 1860 年代以来就一直存在，在该地区发现金矿后吸引了探矿者。

纽约：76 年老房子，塔潘

Old '76 House 的网站声称它的历史可以追溯到 1668 年，而其他消息来源则显示该酒吧建于 1750 年代。 独立战争期间，酒吧充当安全屋。

该酒吧也被称为“安德烈监狱”，曾关押过英国陆军少校约翰·安德烈，后来他因与本尼迪克特·阿诺德密谋并监视美军而被处决。

新泽西州：黑马酒馆和酒吧，Mendham

虽然后来成为 Barnsboro Inn 的小木屋建于 1720 年，但直到 1776 年才成为小酒馆。

剩下的就是门德姆 (Mendham) 的黑马酒馆和酒吧 (Black Horse Tavern & Pub)，该酒馆建于 1742 年。 据《新泽西月刊》报道，这也是该州历史最悠久、持续营业的餐厅。

当它建成时，马厩就矗立在酒吧现在所在的地方，而小酒馆则位于该地产的相邻建筑中。

北卡罗来纳州：鹿角酒吧、吹岩

前任“最古老酒吧”称号的持有者是老塞勒姆的 The Tavern，建于 1816 年。 然而，它于 2019 年关门了。

Antlers 酒吧于 1932 年在 Blowing Rock 开业，现在被认为是该州最古老的酒吧。

Antlers Bar 在最近的一场火灾中被烧毁，但其业主计划完全重新开放。 据其网站称，该酒吧目前由附近的姐妹餐厅 Hellbender Bed and Beverage 运营。

北达科他州：西法戈市政厅酒吧

Peacock Alley American Grill 于 1933 年开业，最近关闭，西法戈的 Town Hall Bar 成为北达科他州最古老的酒吧。

据 KVRR 称，该酒吧于 1935 年建成并开业。

俄亥俄州：Ye Olde Trail Tavern，黄泉

黄泉 (Yellow Springs) 的 Ye Olde Trail Tavern 是由 Elisha Mills 和他的儿子 William 于 1827 年建造的一家小酒馆。 据《黄泉新闻》报道，这里以其招牌汉堡而闻名，据说还有一名身穿蓝色连衣裙的黑发女子经常出没。

俄克拉荷马州：Eischen's Bar，奥卡什

Peter Eischen 于 1896 年创立了 Eischen's Bar。 据酒吧网站称，该酒吧在 1907 年国家禁酒令开始时关闭，但后来由艾森的儿子和孙子重新开业。

据 Yelp 报道，受欢迎的菜肴包括炸鸡、炸薯条派和烤牛肉三明治。

俄勒冈州：Pioneer Saloon，佩斯利

据俄勒冈公共广播公司报道，在俄勒冈州，最古老的律师问题一直备受争议。 佩斯利 (Paisley) 的 Pioneer Saloon 和彭德尔顿 (Pendleton) 的 Rainbow Cafe 两家酒吧均声称于 1883 年开业。

虽然其中任何一个都可以配得上最古老的酒吧称号，但 OPB 报道称，一位历史学家发现了 Pioneer Saloon 的一份遗产记录，证实了 1883 年的日期。 酒吧本身就充满了历史，就像它的 Brunswick 酒吧一样，它是 1905 年从波士顿运来的。

宾夕法尼亚州：乔治二世国王旅馆，布里斯托尔

据 KYW 新闻电台报道，同样于 1681 年开业的 Broad Axe Tavern 于 2019 年关闭。 这使得乔治二世国王旅馆成为该州最古老的旅馆。

据品酒桌报道，乔治·华盛顿的军官曾入住该旅馆，一名宾夕法尼亚州民兵将军帮助计划在旅馆内穿越特拉华河。

罗德岛州：白马酒馆，纽波特

纽波特的白马酒馆 (White Horse Tavern) 被《Condé Nast Traveler》杂志称为“美国最古老的酒吧”。 据酒吧网站介绍，白马酒馆是国家历史地标，最初是一座两层楼的住宅。

1673 年，威廉·梅耶斯 (William Mayes) 将其改为酒馆，并在此举行市议会会议和法庭诉讼。 20 世纪，经过长期忽视后，纽波特县保护协会修复了该财产。

南卡罗来纳州：亨利在市场上，查尔斯顿

该州之前最古老的酒吧是位于查尔斯顿的 McCrady's Tavern and Long Room，其历史可以追溯到 1788 年，但于 2020 年关闭。

虽然亨利市场 (Henry's on the Market) 的历史并不那么悠久，但它自 1933 年就开始营业了。

据酒吧网站介绍，亨利酒吧最初是由德国移民亨利·奥托·哈塞尔迈尔 (Henry Otto Hasselmeyer) 创建的一家杂货店。 禁酒令结束后，他把它变成了一家啤酒店。

南达科他州：布法罗酒庄、戴德伍德

据戴德伍德市称，Buffalo Bodega 成立于 1877 年，以业主的朋友兼狩猎伙伴 Buffalo Bill Cody 的名字命名。

田纳西州：Springwater Supper Club & Lounge，纳什维尔

Springwater 于 1896 年开业，是一家“最纯粹的真正的潜水酒吧”，该酒吧的人才买家杰西·贝克 (Jesse Baker) 告诉《商业内幕》。

尽管在过去的 100 多年里，酒吧的结构不断更新，但仍有大量证据证明其迷人的历史。 贝克说，在禁酒令期间，这家酒吧作为地下酒吧经营，如今，它仍然有一个窥视门，上面有消防队强行闯入“砍头”时留下的斧头痕迹。

德克萨斯州：奥斯汀 Scholz 花园

据 Scholz Garten 网站介绍，Scholz Garten 的酒吧由德国移民、内战老兵 August Scholz 于 1866 年创立。 它很快成为该地区其他德国移民最喜欢去的地方。

1979 年，当这家酒吧被列入国家历史名胜名录时，《纽约时报》报道称，“就酒吧而言，这家酒吧一点也不寻常，它长期充当酒吧、辩论论坛、社区中心和政治集结地。”

如今，这家供应德国美食和烧烤的酒吧深受德克萨斯大学学生的欢迎。

犹他州：流星沙龙，亨茨维尔

据《盐湖论坛报》报道，该酒吧于 1879 年开业。

如今，它装饰着来自世界各地游客的小饰品和钞票，但最引人注目的是巴克的毛绒玩具头，这是一只创纪录的重达 298 磅的圣伯纳犬，据《犹他故事》报道，巴克于 1957 年去世后被安装在墙上。

佛蒙特州：Ye Olde Tavern，曼彻斯特

Ye Olde Tavern 的历史可以追溯到 18 世纪——外面的一块牌子上写着“自 1790 年以来的美酒与餐饮”——尽管此后它已经经历了许多名字和所有者。 自 1976 年以来，它一直使用现在的名称。

据酒馆网站称，该镇的第一条电话线安装在酒馆内。 这座历史建筑现已列入佛蒙特州历史名胜名录。

弗吉尼亚州：阿宾登酒馆

弗吉尼亚州的其他一些历史建筑也是酒吧的所在地，这引发了关于哪一座是最古老的争论。 例如，米德尔堡的红狐旅馆 (Red Fox Inn) 据报道成立于 1728 年，但其国家史迹名录申请中列出的建造日期约为 1830 年。

据 WCYB Abingdon 报道，该酒馆建于 1779 年，通常被认为是弗吉尼亚州最古老的酒吧。 内战期间，它被用作医院，还设有邮局、面包店、理发店和杂货店等。

华盛顿：比克尔顿蓝鸟旅馆

虽然对于谁能获得华盛顿最古老酒吧的称号还存在一些争议，但根据该镇的网站，比克尔顿的 Bluebird Inn 酒吧于 1887 年开业。 据该镇 Alder Creek Pioneer Carousel 博物馆介绍，酒吧在 20 世纪 60 年代首次欢迎女性。

根据 2020 年人口普查，该镇因一年中大部分时间都在此栖息的蓝知更鸟而被称为“世界蓝知更鸟之都”，但人口仅有 90 人。

西弗吉尼亚州：北端酒馆和啤酒厂，帕克斯堡

North End Tavern and Brewery 于 1899 年开业，是该州最古老的酒馆。 据《西弗吉尼亚州公报邮报》报道，原来酒吧的唯一残留物是“铺设在地下室地板上的粗糙砖块”和“地基的一部分”。

20 世纪 90 年代，业主 Joe Roedersheimer 增建了一家啤酒厂。 如今，该酒吧更广为人知的名字是“The Net”。

威斯康星州：地标 1850，密尔沃基

据 OnMilwaukee 报道，该酒吧最初是密尔沃基和拉辛之间的驿马车站。 据《密尔沃基哨兵报》报道，该酒吧于 1850 年开业，最初是一家为农民和游客服务的酒吧。

该建筑于1983年进行了翻修。

怀俄明州：Miners and Stockmen's Steakhouse，哈特维尔

矿工和畜牧业者 (Miners and Stockmen) 于 1862 年首次开业，距怀俄明州建州 28 年。 根据普拉特县的说法，它恰好位于怀俄明州现存最古老的合并城镇哈特维尔。

据酒吧网站介绍，顾客可以从牛排馆菜单以及一长串的葡萄酒和威士忌中进行选择。
